delta_reviews.summary: All four main displays now share formats, controls and routing. Old MAP/config/SFM selections are inactive. This is a source integration improvement, not runtime display qualification.

updates.current: All four main displays now use one format contract and the same format library; page state and rendered formats are routed centrally.
updates.explanation: Replaces earlier primary-only page mapping. Common registration and format-library call paths were read; shared implementation does not prove in-game rendering.

updates.current: One shared controller owns every main bezel, sends blank keys nowhere, and remembers the originally forwarded action so release returns to that owner.
updates.explanation: Replaces split local-versus-forwarded primary page ownership; held release and power-loss quench are now explicit.

updates.current: Each display keeps independent selected page, last page and subview; entering MENU records its prior page and RTN uses that memory.
updates.explanation: Current controller replaces the former single primary menu-return state.

updates.current: Any main bezel press sends focus for that panel; common sensor-control routing recognizes the displayed format on each main screen.
updates.status: Positive routing change; downstream authority needs qualification
updates.explanation: The sensor delta separately checks whether downstream radar axes honor the expanded focus domain. Page routing alone cannot qualify cursor authority.

updates.current: Display page and subview are independent per panel; stores/nav/defensive presentation is parameterized by panel, while underlying sensor and aircraft state remain shared.
updates.status: Explicit policy present; concurrent-input qualification required
updates.explanation: Supersedes the earlier unresolved mirror policy. Verify independent views versus shared edits and the global A/G DATA request arbitration.

updates.current: The old MAP file remains in the tree, but current common format registration excludes it and the controller forces PMFD_MAP_PAGE to zero. No active cartographic moving-map chain is established.
updates.explanation: Do not describe the earlier CLASSIFIED page as currently selectable. NAV route graphics and a cartographic moving map remain separate capabilities.

updates.current: The current common checklist still displays the cold-start texture; bezel labels now come from the common control contract.
updates.explanation: Appearance/control refactoring does not add phase selection, abnormal checklists or automatic completion sensing.

updates.current: The old SFM telemetry file remains as inactive source; current common registration excludes it and the controller forces its visibility flag to zero.
updates.status: Inactive utility; no active equipment credit
updates.explanation: Supersedes the earlier active telemetry-format wording. Obsolete assets are not active aircraft systems.

updates.current: Avionics brightness still permits a broad APU-spool availability path, but the new shared main-display router is explicitly powered by MAIN_POWER.
updates.explanation: A bright surface and a powered selectable format are separate gates. Qualify APU-only startup and supply restoration rather than counting opacity as usable avionics.

updates.current: The active ICP now routes to UFC_Controller. Numeric entries wait for readback with a one-second timeout; the former AP/ALT helper wheel-increment path is no longer the active owner.
updates.explanation: Supersedes the old wheel/draft-specific implementation description. Verify only the currently exposed controls and preserve explicit cancel/commit/pending behavior.

updates.current: Native barometric failure after pressure-request adoption still makes the AFCS frame unhealthy. However, the new active UFC explicitly presets selected altitude from geometric getSelfCoordinates altitude before BALT, or HDG/NAV engagement from AP OFF. AFCS feedback uses indicated barometric altitude, creating a source-datum mismatch when the two differ.
updates.status: Existing source-loss guard retained; new UFC target-source mismatch confirmed in source
updates.explanation: The 01:44 initialization-edge concern is now supplemented by a more concrete 02:38 issue: UFC capture uses geometric height even with healthy native baro. That can command an unintended altitude change instead of capturing current indicated altitude. It does not remove the existing stale-native guard.
updates.acceptance: At stable level flight with QNH chosen so indicated barometric altitude differs substantially from geometric ASL, select UFC BALT and then repeat HDG/NAV from AP OFF. Captured target and feedback must share the intended datum, with no unintended climb/descent. Separately retain the stale-native-after-adoption and pre-adoption failure trials.
updates.proposal: Capture BALT from the same fresh indicated-barometric contract used by AFCS feedback. Keep geometric altitude only as a separately declared assistance/reversion source.

updates.current: From AP OFF, EFM HDG and NAV selections still engage Altitude on the vertical axis. The new active UFC first captures geometric own altitude and sends it as an explicit altitude preset before those selections; direct keybindings can therefore follow a different target-capture path.
updates.status: Source-confirmed combined-axis policy with new interface-dependent target capture
updates.explanation: This expands rather than removes the implicit-ALT finding. The UFC may overwrite a prior altitude preset while direct HDG/NAV commands preserve it through the EFM preset logic. The control interface must not silently determine a different captured datum/target.
updates.acceptance: While climbing with AP OFF and a prior altitude preset present, engage HDG/NAV by UFC and direct binding. Verify the documented pitch mode, preserved/overwritten target and datum for both routes; resolve unexplained differences.
updates.proposal: Publish one mode/target transition table across UFC and HOTAS/keybinding entry points; explicitly define whether an existing altitude preset is retained or current indicated altitude is captured.

updates.current: OBS course remains numerically stored and interpreted using the current true/magnetic reference; toggling the reference can still rotate an already active OBS path. In the final overlay, numeric course commit 10949 now only presets the course and no longer enables OBS automatically. Course increment/decrement and explicit OBS controls still have separate behavior.
updates.status: Source-confirmed active-OBS coupling remains; course-preset separation added

source.match: elseif command==10949 and value>=0 and value<360 then set('F22_NAV_COURSE',value)end

updates.explanation: Credit the removed entry-side activation. Do not say that merely entering CRS now automatically retasks steering. The true/magnetic toggle issue concerns an already active OBS path and is unchanged.
updates.acceptance: Enter a course with OBS OFF: it must remain a preset without changing path. Activate OBS explicitly, establish an intercept at substantial variation, then toggle true/magnetic reference and verify the intended unchanged or deliberately retargeted true course.
updates.proposal: Preserve the new separation of course entry and OBS activation; store course internally in a stable reference or explicitly annunciate any deliberate path redefinition on reference switching.

updates.current: ICP_System now instantiates one UFC_Controller rather than ICP_Flight_Pages. The active controller supports per-field drafts and pending readback for numeric NAV/ALT/HEADING/STORES entries, with page/power cancellation. Its HEADING acknowledgement wrongly applies math.deg to F22_AP_HEADING even though the EFM publishes degrees; a successfully applied heading can therefore time out as NO RESPONSE. Existing-point coordinate commit uses a separate same-ID-only acknowledgement (N10).
updates.status: New active UFC transaction owner; confirmed heading acknowledgement unit mismatch

updates.explanation: The previous positive transaction description cited an obsolete active-owner assumption. Retained helper files do not establish active behavior. The degree/radian mismatch is a deterministic source issue, not a DCS runtime observation.
updates.acceptance: Commit headings 000,090,180 and359 in true and magnetic modes. Verify the achieved target and acknowledgement agree; 000 alone is insufficient because the unit mismatch is hidden there. Then test invalid entry, pending timeout, page switch and power loss without duplicated or misdirected commits.
updates.proposal: Use one explicit unit contract for selected heading and compare readback in that unit. Correlate pending acknowledgements to the setting owner and intended target; keep drafts isolated from committed values.

updates.current: The new active UFC stores/commits waypoint fields through Nav_Entry, with negative-elevation entry still unsupported. For an existing valid point, committing an individual field can send the whole current coordinate tuple immediately. Completion is inferred when HUD_WP_INDEX equals the requested ID; this can be true before the navigation owner processes an edit of that same point, even if it later rejects the coordinates.
updates.status: Field-level commit boundary changed; same-ID-only acceptance is insufficient

additional_sources.match: elseif self.field==4 then if v>65000 then self.error='ELEV 0-65000 FT';return false end;self.alt=v

updates.explanation: This does not make every field-level commit wrong: it requires a documented boundary. The concrete acknowledgement problem is that unchanged selection identity is not proof of a successful edit. Navigation_System already publishes F22_NAV_EDIT_STATUS after checking conversion/storage, but UFC does not use that result for point_wait success.
updates.acceptance: Edit latitude of the currently selected point while deliberately withholding/rejecting navigation conversion or commit. UI must not indicate accepted solely because the point ID stayed the same. Verify applied coordinates/elevation/status for success, rejection, a new point and a changed selected point; specify whether each field or a complete tuple is the commit boundary.
updates.proposal: Add a request sequence and owner result/coordinate readback for waypoint edits. Distinguish field draft, committed tuple and active selection; retain signed-coordinate validation and define negative-elevation support explicitly.

updates.current: The final UFC AP page shows actual active ATTH/HSEL/BALT/RALT/NAV CPL states with colon prefixes, while the EFM keeps target selection and engagement gating separate. The former ICP_Flight_Pages numeric ALT/V/S/CAS/Mach target interface is no longer instantiated; retained files do not prove those fields are currently available on the UFC. V/S and Mach-hold direct bindings remain. AP status/reason text remains drawn on the HUD.
updates.status: Actual-state AP labels added; active UFC control coverage changed and unqualified
updates.explanation: Credit actual state-driven colons. Do not describe the old AP/ALT target-entry pages as active or claim the EFM modes disappeared. New UFC altitude capture has the datum issue in NAV-02; heading success indication has P19 unit mismatch.
updates.acceptance: Inventory each actually reachable AP/AT mode and target control from the final cockpit and bindings. Select unavailable modes and induce source/eligibility loss; actual-state labels and HUD reason must agree, while a stored target or ENTERED label must not imply engagement.
updates.proposal: Keep requested targets and actual modes visibly distinct; provide deliberate cockpit access to the selected supported envelope, or document supported binding-only actions without crediting an uninstantiated helper UI.

updates.current: Navigation mark storage still appends/selects a point and creates direct-to, retasking the active route. The final physical ICP MRK path always sends NAV_SYSTEM mark 10838 and immediately writes MARK STORED status, without checking navigation acceptance; the former ICP A/G mark-sequence side effect is gone. A/G HUD designation remains available through the separate Combat_System ag_mark/SCS route.
updates.status: Source-confirmed retasking retained; MRK semantics changed and success not acknowledged
updates.explanation: This is a control-specific change, not disappearance of all A/G marking. Rejection at route capacity, unavailable ownship data or other failures can leave the new unconditional status misleading.
updates.acceptance: Use ICP MRK in NAV and A/G, with a full route and invalid ownship. Show success only after an actual stored mark; verify intended active-leg change. Separately confirm SCS/HOTAS A/G designation still operates and uses its own target/source contract.
updates.proposal: Define ICP MRK versus sensor designation explicitly. Use navigation-owner acknowledgement before announcing storage, and decide whether store-only should preserve the current route.

The defensive overview currently derives its COAST flag only from RF/optical warning age, so a datalink-only stale target need not receive that C there.
updates.explanation: The longer target lifetime increases the significance of a previously narrow edge: a datalink-only object can remain displayed for up to 62 seconds after prediction stops. Tactical_Situation correctly passes Datalink.position(...).coast to the TSD; Defensive_Overview discards that coast result and calls warning(t), whose coast requires RF or optical observations. This is a source-confirmed cross-page difference, not a simulator flight observation.
updates.acceptance: Compare the same datalink-only object at ages 12,14,30,74 and76 seconds on TSD and defensive overview. Both must distinguish fresh/predicted/held/coasting and remove expired data; a current RF observation must not renew old donor position.
updates.proposal: Propagate datalink position-age/coast into every page that uses its range/position, separately from RF/optical threat-warning coast.

updates.current: Ordinary decoded native reports still set q.time to the local receive callback clock; the custom F22IFDL1 path reads a sender-supplied time from its payload. The75-second retention change did not add an original observation timestamp to ordinary native reports.
updates.explanation: The new comment that original observation time is never renewed is accurate only about not refreshing the stored timestamp during per-frame republication. For ordinary decoded messages the stored time is receipt time. A genuinely new native message receives a new local timestamp, even though the donor observation time is not separately decoded. Do not state that the code now authenticates original measurement age.
updates.acceptance: Delay an ordinary native report and a timestamped peer report. Document which age is known in each path; republication alone must not renew it, and packet reception must not be described as a measured sensor-observation timestamp.
updates.proposal: Retain separate names/provenance for receipt time and available sender-observation time; the full dual-timestamp model is still a proposed improvement.

updates.current: Transmission enable now calls the explicitly resolved setDefaultTransceiversBits export instead of the earlier generic communicator vtable-slot call. Native adapter epoch/reset, receiver and transmitter state paths remain present.
updates.explanation: The resolver binds this export as a required API. This makes the TX-control dependency explicit and supersedes a description limited to a vtable-slot 27 invocation. It does not qualify the complete ABI, radio behavior or multiplayer interoperability.
updates.acceptance: On each supported DCS build, unavailable required exports withdraw READY, enable/disable changes actual transmitter state, and restart/aircraft switch/time reset removes old messages without leaking the terminal.

updates.current: SIL now preserves a frozen mover-display snapshot as well as the image. Cancelling a ground track also normalizes GMTT/SEAT back to GMT/SEA. The radar emission-inhibit publication explicitly includes A/G SIL.
updates.explanation: Frozen movers are captured by hold_image and on ACTIVE-cycle completion, then reused only during silent/non-active frozen state. This avoids clearing/reprojecting the held mover picture as if it were a live scan. Native search remains inhibited through the existing c.active supply/emissions gate. Do not represent held movers as fresh measurements.
updates.acceptance: Enter SIL from MAP/GMT/SEA and active track, move ownship/targets, then use ACTIVE and return to SIL. A held picture retains its source frame, track mode clears coherently, RF emission follows the chosen state, and stale movers are visibly held.

updates.explanation: This closes a visible search-range omission in the callback. It does not establish a detection curve, and the check is horizontal distance, not slant range. Acquisition/tracking still have their own field-of-regard, line-of-sight, response and memory conditions.
updates.acceptance: Place search targets just inside/outside the selected range at different elevation differences, then acquire/track them as they cross the boundary. Verify the documented horizontal/slant convention and independent search/acquisition/track policies.

updates.current: AGR still supplies native terrain range/rate; the final capture explicitly disables native map-video production and map-video display while mode 7 AGR is selected. AGR remains a ranging function, without an object-track or automatic-avoidance implication.

updates.current: A schema 2 source-reference gate now rejects cursor designation when the native frame reference is invalid or its mode, range, expansion or epoch differs from the active controls. The older search/no-video qualification branches still exist after that gate for compatible/older schema paths.
updates.status: Material integration improvement; remaining compatibility qualification
updates.explanation: NativeGroundVideo now publishes schema, mode and range in addition to the existing source pose/expansion/epoch. Thus SC24 must not imply that a ready schema 2 search mode bypasses source-reference matching. It still does not establish a measured image return, an original sensor error model or every fallback condition. Frame publication can lag controls by a render/update boundary and is meant to reject during that mismatch.
updates.acceptance: Attempt designation during mode/range/beam/EXP changes, before the first matching native frame, with no reference, with an old-schema backend, and from a frozen image. Reject mismatched schema 2 frames and explicitly identify any accepted navigation fallback.
updates.proposal: Retain the new matching gate; document the compatibility policy below schema 2 and ensure all image-dependent paths use the actual rendered source frame.

delta_reviews.summary: Final 02:38 MDT capture changes trim ownership and telemetry. All UV01–UV36 material findings remain valid; V02 requires a more specific positive source description. This is source/test review, not a new test run or DCS flight.

updates.current: Later capture adds an owned, time-integrated held-trim controller: pitch 0.04 and roll/yaw 0.02 normalized command units per second; pitch is bounded at ±0.25 and lateral axes at ±0.2. Command 215 stops all trim axes; pitch has a 0.25-second release-settle period. Manual trim inhibits automatic integration only while held/settling, preserves the existing automatic correction during that interval, and no longer transfers or erases it on trim reception. Trim motion requires control power; controller and diagnostic state reset at mission initialization.
updates.status: Source-confirmed improvement / estimated rates / runtime unqualified
updates.explanation: Supersedes the earlier generic trim-ownership description. The 01:44 callback-count increments and persistent manual-trim latch are no longer the active source behavior in the 02:38 capture. Other V/UV flight-law, APU, engine, fuel, hydraulic, brake, gear, oxygen, damage and repair claims remain substantively unchanged. Manufacturer evidence does not authenticate these chosen trim rates or handoff constants.
updates.acceptance: Measure held trim at multiple frame rates and input-repeat rates; verify direction, achieved rate/limits, release, opposing/simultaneous trim commands and the shared stop command. Exercise focus loss, pause, power interruption/restoration, reset, AP trim-disconnect/takeover and approach/refuel configuration changes. Log total pitch command and achieved effectors through the automatic/manual handoff; no unintended step, stuck trim or unannounced restart. Tie any qualification to the exact built DLL and input bindings.
updates.proposal: Retain one authoritative time-based trim owner and its read-only diagnostics. Treat the rates, travel and release settling as declared mod tuning until documented or measured reference evidence supports a change.
